title: Understanding the Web
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of understanding the web in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Clients and servers and HTTP requests and responses.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding the web as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 9 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding the Web matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This topic connects HTTP and IIS configuration to the actual Classic ASP request path. The `.asp` extension alone does not guarantee execution: the relevant IIS feature, application mapping, site binding, physical path, permissions, and provider/runtime dependencies all matter. Diagnose one layer at a time and use a test site rather than changing production defaults blindly.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Clients and servers; HTTP requests and responses; URLs and query strings; Request headers and response headers; Common HTTP status codes. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.expected_output: A request includes a URL and headers; the response includes a status and content type.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect a local request in browser developer tools or use a harmless endpoint. Status and headers are part of the HTTP contract. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Run the example only on a local or test IIS site with the Classic ASP feature enabled. Record the OS, IIS version, site binding, physical directory, and the exact URL used. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of understanding the web. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of understanding the web using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Clients and servers. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

summary: Understanding the Web is one step in the larger Classic ASP request, state, data, security, or maintenance workflow.
The syllabus coverage includes Clients and servers; HTTP requests and responses; URLs and query strings; Request headers and response headers; Common HTTP status codes.
A reproducible legacy-code example records input, environment/version, expected outcome, observed outcome, and a meaningful failure case.
expected_output: A request includes a URL and headers; the response includes a status and content type.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
